title: Evaluation of an impulsivity-focused group intervention in clinical practice for patients with binge eating disorder
summary: First studies hint that a specific psychotherapy that is focusing on impulsivity is able to regulate impulsive loss of control while eating and thus reduce binge eating episodes. These results should now get transmitted to daily clinical practice. We investigate such an impulsivity-focused treatment in clinical practice, where we offer an up to 12 weeks lasting group treatment in our psychosomatic outpatient institute to reduce binge eating episodes in patients with a so-called binge eating disorder. We explore feasability and acceptance of the treatment in the patients and compare frequency of binge eating, eating disorder pathology, impulsivity and depression before and after the treatment.

interventions.name: treatment group: Patients with binge eating disorder who participate in a impulsivity-focused group treatment (9-14 sessions a 60-90 min in biweekly rhythm)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Diagnosis of BED; participation on the outpatient IMPULS treatment; informed written consent
